precepts.text: Ye shall be holy unto me: for I the Lord am holy, and have severed you from other people, that ye should be mine. Holy means severed, separated from all other nations on the face of the earth. So in Colossians 3:12 the Lord is saying it is not all nations.
precepts.point: The Lord through the apostle Paul is instructing the Colossians on how to deal with one another: bowels of mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness, longsuffering, forbearing one another and forgiving one another. Why? Because we are the same people. We are the sons and daughters of the living God, so there is a way we have to govern ourselves and treat each other.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
Colossians 3:12 calls the elect of God “holy and beloved”. Leviticus tells us how to be holy, and who it is for: “And ye shall be holy unto me: for I the Lord am holy, and have severed you from other people, that ye should be mine.”

Holy means severed, separated from all other nations on the face of the earth. He has severed us from other people, “that ye should be mine”: that ye, you Israelites, should be his people.

So right there in Colossians 3:12 the Lord is saying it ain’t all nations. Just in case anyone was confused by what Paul was saying in verse 11, he clears it up in verse 12. The ones told to put on mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness and longsuffering are the holy people, the ones severed from the other nations to be his.

precepts.text: Ye shall be holy unto me, for I the Lord am holy and have severed you from other people. Offered from the floor as the scripture behind being a holy people.
precepts.point: Let the sisters get counsel from sisters. When you do give counsel, it must be what God wants them to hear and beneficial to them, not to your own wants.

note.label: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

precepts.why:
“For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God: the Lord thy God hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself”. He chose you to be special unto him, set apart from everybody else. So the question is: what makes us holy? What scripture?

Leviticus 20:26 was brought from the floor as the answer: “And ye shall be holy unto me: for I the Lord am holy, and have severed you from other people, that ye should be mine.” The Lord is holy, and he severed Israel from other people to be his. That severing is the same set-apart people of Deuteronomy 7:6, chosen “above all people that are upon the face of the earth.”

So there has to be something we are doing that makes us different. We cannot be doing the same thing the world is doing, and we cannot be doing what the churches are doing. What severs us from the other people is the laws of God being applied, which is what Romans 7:12 goes on to show.

precepts.text: Thou hast slain my children to cause them to pass through the fire; that is giving seed unto Molech.
precepts.point: Sin brings judgment on a whole house. Achan coveted the goodly Babylonish garment, the silver, and the wedge of gold, and he and his sons and his daughters and all that he had were stoned and burned in the valley of Achor. What you do is not just about you; your sin can bring judgment on your family.

note.label: Leviticus 20: The Judgments Appointed for the Abominations

precepts.why:
Whosoever of Israel or of the strangers in the land gave of his seed unto Molech was surely put to death; the people of the land stoned him with stones. This is the child sacrifice Ezekiel shows: “thou hast taken thy sons and thy daughters, whom thou hast borne unto me, and these hast thou sacrificed unto them to be devoured.”

“Is this of thy whoredoms a small matter, That thou hast slain my children, and delivered them to cause them to pass through the fire for them?” That is giving seed unto Molech: slaying the children of the Most High and delivering them to pass through the fire. It defiled His sanctuary and profaned His holy name, and Leviticus 20 appoints death for it.

precepts.text: If a soul hear swearing and is a witness and do not utter it, he shall bear his iniquity; wickedness seen must be exposed.
precepts.point: Sin brings judgment on a whole house. Achan coveted the goodly Babylonish garment, the silver, and the wedge of gold, and he and his sons and his daughters and all that he had were stoned and burned in the valley of Achor. What you do is not just about you; your sin can bring judgment on your family.

note.label: Leviticus 20: The Judgments Appointed for the Abominations

precepts.why:
“if the people of the land do any ways hide their eyes from the man, when he giveth of his seed unto Molech, and kill him not”, the Most High set His face against that man and against his family. Looking away is not an option.

“if a soul sin, and hear the voice of swearing, and is a witness, whether he hath seen or known of it; if he do not utter it, then he shall bear his iniquity.” A witness that holds his peace bears iniquity. When you see wickedness you must utter it and expose it.

precepts.text: Achan's covetousness brought stoning and fire on him and his whole house; one man's sin judged his family.
precepts.point: Sin brings judgment on a whole house. Achan coveted the goodly Babylonish garment, the silver, and the wedge of gold, and he and his sons and his daughters and all that he had were stoned and burned in the valley of Achor. What you do is not just about you; your sin can bring judgment on your family.

note.label: Leviticus 20: The Judgments Appointed for the Abominations

precepts.why:
The Most High set His face “against that man, and against his family.” Sin brings judgment on a whole house, and Achan is the proof.

Achan confessed: “When I saw among the spoils a goodly Babylonish garment, and two hundred shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold of fifty shekels weight, then I coveted them, and took them; and, behold, they are hid in the earth in the midst of my tent.” Joshua and all Israel took Achan “and the silver, and the garment, and the wedge of gold, and his sons, and his daughters, and his oxen, and his asses, and his sheep, and his tent, and all that he had: and they brought them unto the valley of Achor.” “And all Israel stoned him with stones, and burned them with fire.”

One man’s covetousness brought stoning and fire on him and his whole house. What you do is not just about you; your sin can bring judgment on your family.

precepts.text: The law of the woman put apart in her issue; chapter 20 judges what chapter 15 defines.
precepts.point: The nakedness of the mother's sister and the father's sister is near kin; they bear their iniquity. He that lies with his uncle's wife or takes his brother's wife, they shall die childless.

note.label: Leviticus 20: The Judgments Appointed for the Abominations

precepts.why:
“if a man shall lie with a woman having her sickness, and shall uncover her nakedness; he hath discovered her fountain, and she hath uncovered the fountain of her blood: and both of them shall be cut off from among their people.” Her sickness is her menstrual cycle.

Chapter 15 defines what chapter 20 judges: “if a woman have an issue, and her issue in her flesh be blood, she shall be put apart seven days: and whosoever toucheth her shall be unclean until the even.” She is put apart; to lie with her in that time is to discover her fountain, and both are cut off.
